statements.statement: A single misplaced punch card could require the programmer to start the entire job over.
statements.explanation: Punch cards had to be in the correct order with the correct hole patterns. A misplaced or incorrect card meant the whole stack had to be corrected and re-fed into the machine.

statements.statement: Punch card programmers could see their results instantly on a screen.
statements.explanation: There were no screens in the punch card era. Programmers fed stacks of cards into room-sized machines and waited hours for results.

statements.statement: Each hole pattern on a punch card represented one instruction for the computer.
statements.explanation: Programmers encoded instructions by punching specific patterns of holes into cards. Each pattern corresponded to a particular instruction the machine could execute.
